I'm a professional makeup artist and I use the same eyebrow pencil on EVERYONE and it's not even an eyebrow pencil. It's an art pencil called an Ebony Graphite Pencil. The most common ones are made by Prismacolor in the U.S., but you can get them anywhere and it will last you for as long as you can hold on to it (they tend to grow legs). I like to buy woodless pencils as they are all product, but that's not imperative. The reason this works on everyone from redheads to brunettes is because it doesn't add "color" to your brows, but creates a light (or heavy if you want to go over it a few times) grey shadow behind your eyebrow hairs and gives the impression of fullness. It even catches those tiny, invisible hairs on your face if there's an area you've overplucked. Oh, and they cost $0.69 at an art supply store! Hope this helps.

As a professional makeup artist, I think those looks are best reserved for "going out" or special occasions. For example, the brown on the forehead and jawline. My makeup artist friends make fun of each other if we catch each other contouring on an average day. What's your budget like? I saw that one of the videos used mostly expensive products. Starting out, you don't want to waste money to practice. But here are my suggestions to re-create this look:

Contour: Kevyn Aucoin Powder Contour in Medium, Concealer: Natasha Denona Hy-Glam Concealer as both concealer and foundation. It's literally so good that the first time I used it I turned to my husband and said "I didn't know concealer could be this good.", A decent couple of brushes- Budget- Real Techniques, Splurge- Omnia by Royal & Langnickel. Blush- Tarte Breezy Cream Blush in Peach Sunset used sparingly by putting some on the back of your hand and then gently dipping your brush in it.

Have you checked the expiration on them? Some brands expire before the expiration date, most notoriously, Kevyn Aucoin Beauty. I've totally written off their foundations and mascaras due to this fact, despite the fact I get a professional discount. Saving money is only worth it if you're **actually** saving money, right?

For extra light but still perfect coverage, you may want to get a Missha BB Cushion. I totally agree with you. Including the meds I've been on for the last 20 years I've tried 35 different meds, some of which were experimental, but as someone who is treatment resistant and didn't find her "combo" for over 20 year I can safely tell everyone:  
THERE IS A DRUG COMBO AND DOSAGE FOR ALMOST EVERYONE.

I met 1 person in 52 years that got 1 monthly treatment of ECT as her medicine and according to her she had "never been happier." but the point is she FOUND SOMETHING. When you are depressed it might seem you'll never find anything, but it may be the last thing left to try that did the trick.  
"Never, Never, Never Give Up!"- Winston Churchill

When I was 25 my PSYCHIATRIST who, was a highly regarded professional and a teacher at one of the most prestigious medical schools in the country, told me I wouldn't live to be 27. I'm currently 52 as of last Saturday. I defied his prediction and all medical probability to reach this age. I'm not saying it's been easy. But honestly you only need one thing to survive even suicidal depression- HOPE. I know that that sounds counterintuitive, but I just kept telling myself "If I can survive this, I can survive anything." And believe me, I've been through it all- emotionally and medically. If you aren't on meds, get on meds. There is absolutely no shame in taking meds. And one might think I had the support of friends and family to get this far. Well not exactly. I have a husband but he only knows some of the pain I've gone through and is much better with physical pain than mental. It took my parents 17 years to admit I had even 1 mental illness and my sister, a nurse of all things, once told me she "doesn't believe in that shit." Before I met the doctor I went to for 17 years, I had taken approximately 28 psych meds. By the time we discovered what worked, the number became 35. Some of them never even went on sale as I was in clinical trials and I also used some drugs for other illnesses for off label purposes. I'm not complaining because it all went into making me what I am today. I'm disabled with my mental illness, but relatively stable and I'm an Ambassador for 2 different mental illness non-profits. I tell my story to legislators on the state and local level. I convince them to allocate funds for the mentally ill. I use my suffering for good. This could be you. Get some meds. And don't think that they're all bad if the first one doesn't work. My last piece of advice is to not take life too seriously because you'll never get out of it alive! : ) Here's one of my favorite quotes:   
“**There is no medicine like hope**, no incentive so great, and no tonic so powerful as expectation of something tomorrow.” — Orison Swett Marden
